correctness.rationale: The distance potential reduces exactly to a two-orbit system with equatorial chord sum n s_n, cross-distance T=sqrt(1+h^2) and apex separation 2h. Solving n s_n a+2Tb=nTa+2hb and na+2b=1 yields a=(T-h)/(nd), b=(T-s_n)/(2d), d=2T-h-s_n; direct full distance-matrix solutions independently match sample n,h and both signs. The strict negative type of Euclidean distance on zero-mass finite signed measures supplies uniqueness and maximizing energy; Gaussian Fourier positivity also extends this to compact finite signed Borel measures. The inequality 2sqrt(1+h^2)-h >= sqrt(3)>4/pi>s_n prevents singular denominators. Monotonic x cot x, cotangent expansion and constant-potential circle integration establish thresholds h_n, their n^-2 approach, and unique circle-plus-poles maximizer. Weak convergence is for fixed h only and does not assert a uniform rate for all continuous tests.
